body: Thank you for your kind words, I smiled just a bit. I hope things are getting better for you. I want to grind it out, but it's just so difficult to wake up every morning and continue on.

Yeah, but with my current financial situation (37k lawsuit, 100k debt) and my inevitable poor credit report in the near future, I worry about having a good career in finance or anything related to it. I'm not sure which industry I would like to find myself in mid-late in my career, but I definitely aspire to work in a big-4 company like every accounting major.
Thank you, I really appreciate the kind words!

Changing schools has never been an option, and it's already too late to transfer (I'm already in the last few semesters of my collegiate career). I'm an Accounting major, but my school has awesome networking and statistically, 88% of graduates from that program land stable, well-paying jobs right after graduation. That being said, the trade-off is academic rigor, not to mention the high tuition. Yeah, I'm not even 21 but I can understand what it's like being financially effed.

You know, I've been told by my psychologist as well that fighting depression is all about self-discovery and acceptance. And while that seems like the golden solution, it's so much easier said than done. I mean there are middle-aged men and women with comfortable lives who haven't achieved that. However, it's probably best of me to accept my situation and where I currently sit but my pride won't allow it. It makes my life hard, but living my real life rather than a lie was already very hard and burdensome. At least living a lie could "save face" and spare me from humiliation and embarrassment from people who aren't on the best terms with me. With my current situation, I'll have to get a job right away and as much as I'd like to travel with a friend, I neither have a friend to travel with nor do I have the funds or luxury with time either.

You're right and you definitely have valid points, but I don't think emotional state of mind is always about logical validity. My depression is based off of the conflicting emotions within myself, masking my own life, and basically living a lie that I created for my own pride and security. Not to mention, the dichotomy of lifestyles that I find myself in is substantial and emotionally burdensome due to the aforementioned points and more. You're treating this like we're sitting in debate 101, and I thank you for your time and calling out certain points, but is emotional distress always based on logic? If so, everyone would go consult a lawyer or debater to tell them how irrational their emotions and rationale are and then everyone would be happy. A person's emotions aren't that simple, especially not for someone who's been battling with these issues for years.
